clue.text: Order unhealthy food for one to tuck into?

indicators.note: to tuck into a meal is to put it inside you, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: fat is the food a dietitian warns against
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone picks junk food off a menu to eat themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a request to a waiter, but it is the definition, in its sense of a command; 'for one' tells you the I is the one doing the eating.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiat is an authoritative decree or command, the same as an order handed down from above.

clue.text: Odds on wet weather bringing physical injury

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the betting odds when a race begins
the commonest wet weather

explanation.surface: A bookmaker's odds on a rainy day, and a fall on slippery ground.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, short for starting price, is the racecourse abbreviation for the odds; 'on' simply places the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprain is a twisted or wrenched joint, a common bodily injury to ankles or wrists.

clue.text: Customer's first request — quantity of beer?

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
to ask is to request

explanation.surface: A pub customer's opening request at the bar is about how much beer to pour.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: a cask is a container, and here stands for the amount of beer it holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A cask is a barrel, and the beer filling one is a standard measured amount in the brewing trade.

clue.text: Hippy so hearty after manipulation — treatment to improve movement?

indicators.note: manipulation means handling and moving things about, so the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: the thirteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A hippy feels so well after a massage, as if the treatment loosened them up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manipulation' is doubly apt: physiotherapists manipulate joints, and the setter manipulates the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Physiotherapy treats injury and stiffness with exercise and massage, aiming to restore a patient's mobility.

clue.text: Fellow at home entertaining the French minister

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to take them into your house, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
someone at home is in
la is French for the, feminine form

explanation.surface: A man at home hosts the French minister for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The French minister' reads as one political figure, but 'the French' is LA and 'minister' alone is the definition; LA goes into CHAPIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a clergyman attached to a college, regiment or hospital, so a minister of religion.

clue.text: Strangers beginning to assert legal rights

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
a lien is a legal right to keep someone's property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: Foreigners start insisting on their rights in law.
explanation.walkthrough: A lien is a lawyer's word: the right to hold goods against an unpaid debt, as a garage may hold a repaired car.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliens are foreigners or outsiders, people unfamiliar or from elsewhere, which is what strangers are.

clue.text: Clothes ink spoilt and water ruined

indicators.note: something spoilt has been damaged out of its proper shape, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked and broken up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A garment is ruined by spilt ink and a soaking.
explanation.walkthrough: Each word is scrambled separately and the results joined; 'Clothes' looks like part of the laundry disaster but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Knitwear covers jumpers, cardigans and other knitted garments, a category of clothing.

clue.text: Charge every individual backing mischief-maker

indicators.note: to back someone is to stand behind them, so one piece follows the other

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child or sprite
each means every one taken individually

explanation.surface: Every person in the room supports the troublemaker, and a charge is laid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' here does not turn letters round: it means supporting from behind, so the piece for everyone comes after the troublemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: To impeach a public official is to formally accuse them of misconduct, bringing a charge against them.

clue.text: Girl making Rachel envious to some extent

indicators.note: only to some extent means only partly, so just a portion of the letters is used

parts.note: the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: One girl is making her friend Rachel jealous.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle the end of the name and the start of 'envious'.
explanation.definitionFit: Helen is a common female given name, and crosswords use 'girl' for any girl's name.

clue.text: Go after vehicle returning with king

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a cart is a simple vehicle
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Pursue the car coming back with the monarch inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The vehicle is turned round before the king is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To track someone is to follow their trail and pursue them, so to chase or go after them.

clue.text: Wise, misconstrued as "inept"

indicators.note: to misconstrue is to read something wrongly, putting it in the wrong arrangement

parts.note: the seven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A wise person is wrongly taken for a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' looks like a link word but is part of the letters to rearrange, with 'inept'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapient is a formal, rather literary adjective for having great knowledge and good judgement.

clue.text: Time messenger comes with duck and fruit

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
angel comes from the Greek for messenger, God's messenger
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, so the round letter

explanation.surface: A courier arrives on time bringing a duck and some fruit, perhaps for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricketer out without scoring has made a duck, and nought looks like O.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangelo is a citrus hybrid of tangerine and pomelo or grapefruit, a kind of fruit.

clue.text: The son, affectedly religious, an actor

parts.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for son
pi is schoolboy slang for pious, showily devout
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sanctimonious son turns out to be a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, short for pious, is British slang for someone ostentatiously or sanctimoniously religious.
explanation.definitionFit: Thespian, from Thespis the Greek dramatist, is a slightly jocular word for an actor or actress.

clue.text: Huge animal damaged a net — help!

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the eight letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A giant beast has torn through a net and someone calls for assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: The cry for aid is not an exclamation in the cryptic reading: its letters join the net's in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: The elephant is the largest living land mammal, so the obvious huge animal.

clue.text: Man maybe at the east side of a passage

indicators.note: east is the right-hand side of a map, so this piece is written to the right

parts.note: taken as written
the Isle of Man is an example of an isle, hence 'maybe'

explanation.surface: A man stands at the eastern end of a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is capitalised at the start, hiding that it means the Isle of Man, the island between Britain and Ireland; in an across answer, east means after.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats or shelves, a narrow passage.

clue.text: Left work in the middle of week to go to Gretna Green?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
the middle of a word is its central letters, with the ends dropped

parts.note: the two central letters of the word
L is the abbreviation for left
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Someone walks out of the office midweek to get married in secret.
explanation.walkthrough: Gretna Green is a Scottish border village where English couples fled to marry without parental consent; the question mark marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run away secretly to marry, and Gretna Green was the classic destination for such runaway weddings.

clue.text: More than one mammal staggers with head hidden

indicators.note: a hidden head is out of sight, so the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: to potter is to move about aimlessly or unsteadily

explanation.surface: An animal reels about, ducking its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staggers' must be read as a verb meaning wanders unsteadily, giving the word before its first letter is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Otters are aquatic mammals of the weasel family, and the plural answer matches 'more than one'.

clue.text: German city worker cut short series of deliveries

indicators.note: cutting something short trims off its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled by one bowler

explanation.surface: A delivery worker in a German city has their round shortened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliveries' suggests post, but these are balls bowled in cricket, six to an over.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanover is a major city in northern Germany, capital of Lower Saxony.

clue.text: Bag is buried in valley

indicators.note: something buried lies inside the ground around it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a vale is a valley
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bag lies buried somewhere in a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: VALE is the poetic word for valley, and it surrounds the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: A valise is a small travelling case or suitcase, a kind of luggage bag.

clue.text: One throwing large jug

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the baseball player who throws the ball to the batter
second meaning: a big jug with a lip and handle for pouring

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as someone hurling a big jug; the two halves are independent meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball the one who throws is the pitcher, and a pitcher is also a large pouring jug.

clue.text: Under arch, offering accommodation for the Spanish

indicators.note: to accommodate a guest is to house them, so one piece holds another

parts.note: a bow is a curved arch shape
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Beneath an archway, lodging is offered to Spaniards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under arch' looks like a single phrase, but 'Under' alone is the definition and the arch is the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Below and under both mean in a lower position than something, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Sounding unhappy, exhaled forcefully

indicators.note: sounding points to how a word is said rather than spelt

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling sad

explanation.surface: Someone sighing heavily sounds miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: The sad colour word and the past tense of the verb to blow are pronounced identically.
explanation.definitionFit: Blew is the past tense of blow, which means to send out air hard from the mouth.

clue.text: Some new idea of great scope

indicators.note: some means only a part, so just a portion of the letters is used

parts.note: the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A fresh concept with ambitious reach.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters bridge the end of 'new' and the start of 'idea'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wide in range covers a lot, as in wide-ranging; great scope is broad extent.

clue.text: Professional wearing an outer garment for protection

indicators.note: someone wearing clothes is inside them, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: taken as written
pro is short for professional

explanation.surface: A tradesman puts on an overall to keep their clothes clean.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'an outer garment' a single phrase, but 'an' goes around the professional and the rest is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is tied over the front of clothes to shield them from dirt or spills while working.

clue.text: Delighted editor backing requests

indicators.note: to back something is to stand behind it in support, so one piece comes after the other

parts.note: pleas are earnest requests
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A happy editor supports the appeals sent in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' does not turn letters round here: it means supporting from behind, so the editor goes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleased and delighted both describe feeling happy and satisfied with something.
